name: Canonical FastAPI/Starlette middleware order and security headers
short_definition: Canonical cross-cutting ASGI middleware stack for FastAPI services: correct add_middleware order (last added = outermost), CORS, TrustedHost, HTTPS redirect (when appropriate), GZip, proxy headers, request-ID/logging, timeouts, and security response headers. Official FastAPI: middleware forms a stack; request flows outermost→innermost→route; response reverses. Dependencies with yield run after middleware; BackgroundTasks after all middleware.
scope_in: Request ID, structured logging, exception-safe headers
Security headers on API responses (HSTS, nosniff, frame, referrer, permissions)
What belongs in middleware vs Depends vs router dependencies
scope_out: Business authorization rules inside middleware (use Depends)
CSP nonce pipelines for HTML apps (API-first services rarely need full CSP)

defaults.order_rule: Last app.add_middleware(X) is outermost; runs first on request, last on response
canonical_outer_to_inner_request: HTTPSRedirectMiddleware (only if app terminates TLS or must force https)
defaults.cors: Explicit allow_origins from settings; allow_credentials only with explicit origins; never * with credentials
defaults.auth: Prefer Depends/APIRouter dependencies for authZ — not giant middleware that parses every path
headers_api: Cache-Control appropriate for authenticated APIs (often no-store)
defaults.expose_custom_headers: Add to CORS expose_headers if browsers must read X-Request-Id etc.

middleware_when: Must run for every request (CORS, host check, request ID, security headers, compression)
Needs raw ASGI access (streaming, early reject)
depends_when: Auth user loading, DB session, tenant context, per-route permissions
Optional dependencies only on some routes
proxy_layer_when: HSTS/TLS and broad security headers often better at ingress/CDN — still set app-level defaults for defense in depth when clients hit app directly
skip_gzip_when: SSE/streaming endpoints where buffering hurts — exclude or set carefully

do: Add CORS outermost among app middlewares that must see preflight early (typical pattern: add CORS last so it is outermost)
Keep middleware pure and fast — no DB in middleware
Propagate X-Request-Id from inbound or generate UUID; bind to structlog context
Document order in main.py comments for agents
Test preflight OPTIONS and credentialed CORS
Use app.add_middleware for third-party ASGI middleware so exception handlers work
dont: Don't implement full session auth only in middleware and skip route checks
Don't mutate response body after streaming started carelessly
Don't trust X-Forwarded-For from the public internet without proxy allowlist
Don't put heavy CPU/crypto in middleware without caching where safe
Don't reverse order casually — last-added is outermost

code_skeleton:
from uuid import uuid4
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.middleware.gzip import GZipMiddleware
from fastapi.middleware.trustedhost import TrustedHostMiddleware
from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
from starlette.types import ASGIApp

# Example settings
ALLOWED_ORIGINS = ["https://app.example.com", "http://localhost:3000"]
ALLOWED_HOSTS = ["api.example.com", "localhost"]

class RequestIdMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next):
        request_id = request.headers.get("x-request-id") or str(uuid4())
        request.state.request_id = request_id
        response = await call_next(request)
        response.headers["X-Request-Id"] = request_id
        return response

class SecurityHeadersMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next):
        response = await call_next(request)
        response.headers.setdefault("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
        response.headers.setdefault("X-Frame-Options", "DENY")
        response.headers.setdefault("Referrer-Policy", "strict-origin-when-cross-origin")
        response.headers.setdefault("Permissions-Policy", "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()")
        # HSTS only when you are sure HTTPS is enforced end-to-end
        # response.headers.setdefault("Strict-Transport-Security", "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload")
        return response

app = FastAPI()

# add_middleware: LAST added = OUTERMOST (runs first on request)
app.add_middleware(GZipMiddleware, minimum_size=1000)
app.add_middleware(SecurityHeadersMiddleware)
app.add_middleware(RequestIdMiddleware)
app.add_middleware(TrustedHostMiddleware, allowed_hosts=ALLOWED_HOSTS)
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=ALLOWED_ORIGINS,
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
    expose_headers=["X-Request-Id"],
)
# Request order: CORS → TrustedHost → RequestId → SecurityHeaders → GZip → route
failure_modes: CORS middleware not outermost → preflight never gets ACAO headers
Middleware order reversed after refactor → subtle prod-only bugs
TrustedHost too strict behind LB with wrong Host header → 400s
Logging middleware reads body and breaks streaming/uploads
Security headers only on HTML apps forgotten for APIs that still get browsed
yield dependencies assumed to run before middleware teardown (docs: yield exit after middleware)
anti_patterns: Auth entirely in middleware with route handlers trusting request.state.user blindly without tests
Dozen middlewares each doing partial auth/rate-limit/logging with unclear order
Copy-pasting Next CSP middleware into FastAPI JSON API without adaption
Catch-all middleware that swallows exceptions and returns 200

versions_as_of.note: Middleware APIs stable; verify CORS/TrustedHost args against current Starlette docs on upgrade

# 1 CORS 2 TrustedHost 3 RequestId 4 SecurityHeaders 5 GZip → routes

deprecation_watch: Custom CORS hacks instead of CORSMiddleware
BaseHTTPMiddleware known caveats for some streaming edge cases — prefer pure ASGI middleware if profiling shows issues
Disabling TrustedHost with allowed_hosts=['*'] on public multi-tenant hosts
ts_boundary: Browser calls from Next (localhost:3000 / app origin) require FastAPI CORS allowlist of that origin when not same-origin proxied. Prefer Next rewrite/proxy to same origin in prod to reduce CORS surface. Cookie SSR auth stays on Next middleware; Python service uses Bearer/service tokens for server-to-server.
rust_boundary: Axum/Tower layer order is analogous (outer layers first). When porting, map CORS/trace/timeout layers explicitly; don't assume middleware names match.
supabase_boundary: If FastAPI validates Supabase JWTs, do it in Depends not CORS middleware. CORS must allow the web app origin only; never reflect Origin arbitrarily. Service-role calls are server-side — no CORS involved.
boundary_contracts: Error JSON still applies security headers
OpenAPI security schemes separate from CORS

decision_matrix_row.problem_class: Cross-cutting HTTP concerns on Python API

threats: CORS misconfiguration → credential theft from browser
Client IP spoofing via X-Forwarded-For → auth bypass of IP allows / rate limit dodge
Clickjacking if API serves any HTML admin
Information leak via verbose CORS/error headers
Cache poisoning if shared caches ignore Cache-Control on auth APIs
mitigations: Explicit CORS origins from env; review on each frontend domain add
Proxy trust allowlist at server layer
Rate limit + auth in Depends after identity established (order: auth then rate limit for user-keyed limits)

must_generate: CORS from settings list not hardcoded * for credentialed apps
Request ID middleware or OTel instrumentation
TrustedHost when deploying with known hostnames
must_not_generate: Middleware that consumes request body for logging on all routes
Gzip on streaming/SSE routes without exclusion

tests_required: Security headers present on JSON error and success
Streaming/SSE still works with stack enabled
ci_gates: Unit/integration tests for CORS and headers
Lint/grep ban allow_origins=["*"] combined with credentials True
Optional: securityheaders scan on staging URL

positive: CORSMiddleware with explicit origins from settings
negative: No CORS but browser frontend on different origin
Missing request id on public API
Custom CORS headers hand-rolled on each route

Canonical: CORS → TrustedHost → RequestId → SecurityHeaders → GZip → routes (adjust with comments)
CORS: explicit origins; never * with credentials
Trust X-Forwarded-* only from proxy CIDRs
yield-deps run after middleware; BackgroundTasks after all middleware (FastAPI docs)

conflicts_noted: Exact middleware ordering recipes vary across blogs; FastAPI documents stack semantics clearly — project-specific order should follow outermost-first needs (CORS/preflight usually outer)
Whether HSTS belongs on app vs CDN: both valid; avoid HSTS on plain HTTP local dev
BaseHTTPMiddleware vs pure ASGI performance/streaming debates in Starlette community — use BaseHTTPMiddleware for simple cases; pure ASGI if issues
